title: Surgical pathology of childhood
objectives: State the histology that confirms Hirschsprung, biliary atresia and Wilms substaging.
List small-round-cell tumour differentials with the immunostain that separates each.
Explain Stocker CPAM types and germ-cell tumour marker patterns.
body_md:
### Why this area matters

Pathology sub-parts sit inside tumour, Hirschsprung, biliary and lung questions. The marks go to named stains, named types and marker patterns — general descriptions score poorly.

### The non-negotiable histologies

Hirschsprung: absent ganglion cells with hypertrophic nerve trunks on rectal biopsy (acetylcholinesterase backup). Biliary atresia: portal-tract fibrosis, bile-duct proliferation and plugs versus neonatal hepatitis patterns. Wilms: favourable versus anaplastic histology drives everything after surgery. CPAM follows Stocker 0–IV by cyst size and cell lining — and the exam separates prenatal ultrasound size classes from pathology types, so name both systems.

### Small-round-cell tumours

Neuroblastoma (Homer-Wright rosettes, N-myc, INPC Shimada), Wilms (triphasic blastemal-epithelial-stromal), rhabdomyosarcoma (embryonal versus alveolar, myogenin/MyoD1), Ewing/PNET (CD99, EWSR1 translocation), lymphoma (LCA). One line each: morphology + the stain or translocation that clinches it. Germ-cell tumours split by age and site with markers AFP (yolk sac), beta-hCG (choriocarcinoma), LDH and PLAP patterns.

### Tumour markers as pathology

AFP half-life tracks yolk-sac response; beta-hCG marks choriocarcinomatous elements; VMA/HVA follow neuroblastoma; NSE is supportive. State what rises, what normalises with cure, and what a plateau means (residual or resistant disease).

### How it is asked

“Under the microscope” sub-parts, marker grids, and classify-then-manage stems. Tables beat paragraphs — stain in the left column, diagnosis on the right.
